review_candidates.title: Coordinator, Digital Health (Ethiopia)
review_candidates.description: This role was posted on August 13, 2026. Please note that we will review applications on a rolling basis. About Last Mile Health Last Mile Health saves lives in the world's most remote communities. Our vision is a health worker within reach of everyone, everywhere. We partner with governments to recruit, train, equip, and integrate professional community health workers into national health systems, equipping them to deliver quality primary care in rural and remote communities. Founded in Liberia in 2007, we now operate programs in Ethiopia, Liberia, Sierra Leone, and Malawi. Our global offices are located in Accra, Ghana and in the United States. We are looking for mission-driven leaders to join us as we work to ensure no patient is out of reach. About The Ethiopia Team The Ethiopia team works in partnership with Ethiopia’s Ministry of Health to strengthen the country’s flagship Health Extension Program, a globally recognized model for delivering primary healthcare through more than 40,000 Health Extension Workers. Led by Abraham Zerihun, the team works to upskill the Health Extension Workers through blended learning that combines digital and in-person training. It also advances digital innovation through HEP Assist, an AI-powered clinical decision-support tool that helps Health Extension Workers provide evidence-based care at the point of service. The team's portfolio spans maternal, newborn, child health, nutrition, and non-communicable diseases, including hypertension, diabetes, eye care, and stroke prevention and management, while strengthening health systems through sustainable community health financing, resource mapping, and strategic planning to support long-term government leadership and program sustainability. The Role At Last Mile Health (LMH), we make bold commitments that inspire innovation. Do you have experience supporting digital health implementation, troubleshooting technology in the field, and working with frontline health workers to deploy and strengthen digital health solutions? If so, you may be the next Digital Health Coordinator at Last Mile Health. The Digital Health Coordinators will provide high level technical and implementation support for the deployment of LMH's digital health tools to Community Health Workers (CHWs) across Ethiopia, including Extension Essentials and HEP Assist AI. Reporting to the Director, Digital Health, Ethiopia, the Coordinators will support planning, coordination, and implementation of digital health activities, working closely with program teams, field teams, and users to ensure effective adoption and use of digital health solutions. Based in Addis Ababa, the role will provide hands-on support to digital health implementation and will travel to different regions as needed to support field deployment and training activities. The Coordinators will support workplan management, data collection and feedback processes, data analysis and dashboard development, application installation and troubleshooting, and the development and implementation of processes and procedures that strengthen digital health activities. The role will also provide remote technical support to users through phone, email, and relevant open source digital health communities. This advertisement is for two Digital Health Coordinator positions based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. This is a fixed-term position for 24–36 months, with the potential for renewal. The role is based onsite in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, and is open only to candidates who are currently located in and authorized to work in Ethiopia. What You'll Do Digital Health Solutions Implementation Coordination Coordinate with the Senior Digital Health Coordinators to ensure that the digital health initiatives are run successfully across all districts Work with the Director, Digital Health, Senior Manager of Digital Health, Ethiopia country office program team, the Global DH Manager, and other relevant internal LMH departments (MERL, HSS, etc.) to maintain and update deployment tasks in the implementation plan Roll out new Deployment Packages (latest apps and tools such as Extension Essentials and HEP Assist AI) to Health Extension Workers (HEWs) Support establishment of a digital health management processes and procedures for digital health activities Support Digital Health Training activities including the planning and deployment of a digital education platform for Health Extension Workers Coordinate, facilitate and participate in health worker and health systems leaders trainings across districts Support learners (health workers, Ministry of Health (MOH) and health system leaders) during training (including app installation on mobile device, etc.) and remotely after training Support LMH and MOH program managers/ Coordinators in creating user accounts for app access and maintain dashboards to track learners sync status and course performance Support data collection efforts for all digital health activities including data tracking, data review and date submission support Ensure that all users have functioning equipment during training and support immediate troubleshooting of devices during activity deployments Support the Director, Digital Health to communicate LMH digital health priorities, and provide training on essential digital health skills to LMH and MoH team members when applicable Test and Innovate New Solutions for The Ethiopian Health Extension Program (HEP) When necessary, update course content in moodle as requested by the Programs team. This may require quick edits, quality assurance, and publishing of course materials. Quality assurance (particularly) regression testing (testing of new features in new releases) of software before launch Feedback provision and gathering on releases (testing releases, post-release) Identify and report bugs through LMH’s tracking systems (Jira), and on the Oppia Mobile Community website Test new plug-ins, alternative learning platforms, and assess the suitability of different digital health software and hardware for the national HEW program Support the Senior Software Engineer to configure learning software and support the integration and migration between systems as requested Understand and troubleshoot technical issues in the field and report them to the Senior Digital Health Coordinators and Senior Software Engineer Brainstorm and test innovations such as experimental hardware, forms, and digital interventions related to LMH’s digital health platform When necessary, participate in field visits to observe digital health team processes (including device management, follow-up data collection, feedback gathering) and generate ideas for improvement Draw on technical skills, critical thinking, problem-solving ability, and creativity to provide the technical edge to LMH’s digital health platform What You'll Bring Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field, such as computer science, Information Technology, software engineering, statistics, mathematics with minimum of three years of work experience. Experience working with data systems including data entry, data quality assurance, and data cleaning, relational databases, dashboard development, and monitoring and evaluation Experience with project management, and a high level of initiative Relevant years of experience working on IT-related projects Progressive years of experience designing and implementing Digital Health systems in the field. Willingness and ability to travel to remote areas of Ethiopia, sometimes for overnight visits You'll Impress Us If You are knowledgeable and experienced with community health systems, especially the Ethiopian Health Extension Workers (HEW) program You have the ability to build and edit courses on Moodle LMS You have experience with analyzing data and developing dashboards using data analytics and visualization tools like Data Studio You have verbal and written communication skills for understanding project requirements and explaining these needs to employees and third-party providers You are able to prioritize and manage time to ensure tasks are completed on time We're looking for someone with many of the qualifications listed above, but we know no one meets every requirement. If you're excited about our mission and believe your experience aligns with this role, we encourage you to apply. Compensation information Overview Of Last Mile Health’s Compensation Model At Last Mile Health, we are committed to equitable and transparent compensation. Employees are paid using a clear, consistent methodology that is fully transparent and accessible to everyone. We look forward to answering any questions you may have during the hiring process. Before applying to this role, please take a moment to learn more about our approach to compensation and how compensation works in each of the countries where we operate. Please find the link to our compensation model and benefits overview below: Compensation For This Position The Band for this position: ETH-2 For Ethiopia, the range is an annual gross of $13,094 USD to $24,733 USD, dependent upon experience doing an equivalent role. Please note that compensation is subject to statutory taxes. Benefits Healthcare: Comprehensive health insurance and wellbeing support for you and your dependents. Save for retirement: Retirement options with a 3% employer match, varying by location. Paid time off: Generous paid time off, sick leave, quarterly company holidays, and approximately one week of office closure at the end of the year. Family support: Generous parental leave for employees welcoming a child through birth or adoption. Professional development: Access to technical and leadership development opportunities to support your growth. Mental healthcare: Counselling and resilience services to support employees and their dependents through life’s challenges. We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at Last Mile Health. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. Last Mile Health is a registered 501(c)3 non-profit organization. For more information, visit www.lastmilehealth.org. At Last Mile Health, we are committed to creating a safe and inclusive environment for everyone. If you require assistance or a reasonable accommodation due to a disability during the selection process, please inform the People Operations team member you are engaging with. Any disclosure related to a disability will be kept strictly confidential and used solely to determine appropriate accommodations. Disclosure is entirely voluntary and will not influence hiring decisions or employment opportunities.

review_candidates.description: Job Description Introduction Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants. IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration Internal and external candidates will be considered for this vacancy. For the purposes of this vacancy, internal candidates are defined as staff members holding a regular, fixed-term or short-term graded or ungraded contract, including Junior Professional Officers (JPOs), staff on Special Leave Without Pay (SLWOP), UN Volunteers with at least twelve (12) months of continuous service in IOM, and staff members on secondment/loan released by the Organization, unless otherwise specified in their contract. Staff members holding a regular, fixed-term or short-term graded contract will not retain their contract type if appointed to an ungraded position. Organizational Context and Scope IOM operates Five Accommodation Centers for Unaccompanied Minors (Shelters) providing accommodation and access to services for Unaccompanied Migrant Children (UMC). Besides accommodation, the following services are provided to the beneficiaries: addressing basic needs, food, hygiene, legal counselling, and information about life opportunities in Greece, interpretation, psychosocial support, m edical support, Greek learning programs, learning support, organization of intercultural activities, work and career guidance. In order to be proactive and be able to cover all urgent staff needs for the shelters on time, we upload vacancies through WAVE for all specialties required for the 24/7 operation of the shelters, aiming to create a pool of suitable candidates. Within the framework of the action "Subsidy N.P. INTERNATIONAL ORGANIZATION FOR MIGRATION (IOM) MISSION GREECE for the implementation of the project "Operation of K.F.A.A. Kypseli I"" with MIS Code 6016486 the Program "Greece Programme - Asylum, Migration and Integration Fund 2021-2027". Under the overall supervision of the National Project Officer or their designate and the direct supervision of the Shelter Coordinator, the successful candidate will perform routine duties related to the assistance, care and provision of services to the UMCs residing in the assigned shelter. Responsibilities Assist in the daily operations of the center, according to the instructions and suggestions of the shelter coordinator and the scientific responsible. Ensure the implementation of the individual daily program of the beneficiaries in collaboration with the social worker; escort children to social and/or medical services when necessary. Provide guidance and support to beneficiaries in maintaining rules of personal hygiene, cleanliness and home economy. Update the coordinator about the adequacy of all necessary materials (personal hygiene items, clothing, footwear, clothing, stationery) and take care of their timely replenishment, receipt, storage, and maintenance. Oversee and prevent any damage to equipment, facilities and building of the accommodation center, while educating minors in their respect and functional use. Maintain and update the entry-exit book of minors and visitors of the center. Handle crisis and emergency situations effectively ensuring timely notification of the scientific staff of the shift or the staff who are on call. Communicate and coordinate with local authorities in case external or internal situations that may threaten the safety of minors and staff. Ensure security of accommodated children on 24-hour shifts, including during night, weekends and public holidays. Perform such other duties as may be assigned. Qualifications Required Qualifications and Experience Education High school degree in Greece or proven attendance at a foreign school. Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database. Experience Experience or training in a subject relevant to child protection, protection of unaccompanied minors, vulnerability management, reception of applicants for international protection or integration of recognized beneficiaries of international protection. Familiar with direct assistance to migrants and/or refugees and particularly with children; Previous experience in a similar role preferred; Experience with diverse populations and cultural sensitivity; Experience working in a multi-cultural environment; Willingness to work on day/night shifts, during holidays and weekends; Positive records of previous experience in a similar field; Valid driver’s license with at least five years of driving experience will be an asset. review_candidates.title: CEO
review_candidates.description: O setor de indústrias de plásticos vivencia um ciclo de evolução estratégica, impulsionado pela busca ininterrupta por eficiência operacional, sofisticação tecnológica e consolidação de mercado. Inserida nessa dinâmica, a organização reafirma sua liderança setorial ao expandir sua capacidade fabril e diversificar sua atuação em segmentos industriais de alta exigência, mantendo padrões rigorosos de qualidade e segurança. Para capitanear esta etapa de crescimento acelerado e fortalecer a rentabilidade institucional em um cenário econômico desafiador, buscamos um Chief Executive Officer (CEO). Como Chief Executive Officer, sua principal missão será liderar a visão estratégica e a evolução contínua da organização, elevando a eficiência operacional e a penetração de mercado em múltiplos polos produtivos. Sob sua gestão estará a condução de um ecossistema industrial diversificado, a proteção das margens do negócio frente a volatilidades setoriais e o fortalecimento de uma cultura corporativa orientada à inovação e à excelência preditiva. Sua liderança será o catalisador para integrar a excelência operacional das unidades à expansão comercial, garantindo o atingimento de novos patamares de lucratividade e valor para os acionistas. Principais Responsabilidades: Dirigir a estratégia global de expansão e governança, assegurando o alinhamento das frentes produtivas, comerciais e financeiras aos objetivos de crescimento da companhia. Blindar a rentabilidade do negócio mediante o redesenho de processos operacionais e a mitigação de barreiras macroeconômicas ou oscilações de mercado. Guiar a evolução cultural da organização, harmonizando diretrizes consolidadas a práticas de gestão contemporâneas e voltadas à inovação industrial. Orquestrar a expansão de market share, identificando oportunidades de diversificação do portfólio de clientes e ampliação da presença em setores de alta tecnologia. Chancelar o plano de investimentos e ampliação da capacidade fabril, garantindo o uso racional de capital e o retorno sobre o patrimônio investido. Consolidar os ecossistemas de qualidade total e segurança, perpetuando indicadores de excelência técnica e relação de alta fidelidade com clientes estratégicos. Unificar a governança do comitê executivo, inspirando líderes multidisciplinares para garantir máxima sinergia entre as diretorias operacionais, comerciais e corporativas. Requisitos: Sólida trajetória executiva na alta liderança corporativa de operações industriais multissite de grande porte, com comprovado domínio sobre os pilares financeiro, comercial e operacional no segmento de injeção plástica e componentes técnicos. Vivência estratégica na condução de planos agressivos de expansão de mercado e na reestruturação de processos produtivos complexos sob cenários macroeconômicos desafiadores. Capacidade comprovada de conduzir transformações culturais e implementar modelos modernos de gestão e inovação em estruturas corporativas consolidadas. Formação executiva de alto nível, aliada a um perfil analítico, visão sistêmica do setor de transformação e disponibilidade total para deslocamentos estratégicos às unidades operacionais. Disponibilidade para residir na Serra Gaúcha, RS.

The analyst partners with IT teams and business users to deliver solutions that support both operational and reporting requirements. The position also works closely with IT, Finance, Controllers and Operations to evaluate and deploy new system features, enhancements, and finance solutions, while identifying gaps between JD Edwards (JDE) EnterpriseOne (E1) and related integrations. Success in this role requires deep enterprise resource planning expertise, particularly in JDE E1 job cost, job profit/recognition, service billing, contract billing, financial modules (AP, AR, Fixed Assets and General Accounting), and the integration points across these functions. Company Overview With roots dating to 1891 and 8,500+ employees, MYR Group Inc. (MYR Group) is a publicly traded holding company of specialty electrical construction companies. MYR Group subsidiaries work on large-scale electrical construction projects throughout the U.S. and Canada. We contribute to a clean energy future while fostering a safe, supportive, and inclusive work environment. Our culture is built on shared values and mutual respect, where teamwork and collaboration occur naturally. Throughout our rich history, we have partnered with utilities, municipalities, commercial clients, and developers to deliver some of the largest and most complex projects, including new construction, upgrades, maintenance and repair for transmission, distribution and substation facilities, commercial and industrial electrical construction, emergency and storm restoration, clean energy, pre-construction services, and engineer-procure-construct (EPC) methods of project delivery. Essential Functions Work closely with Sr. Business Analyst, Developers and other technical team members and business users during project implementations, upgrades, and migrations. Document current and future-state process flows to analyze business processes, including user roles, use cases, edit rules, detailed system and functional specifications. Support business users and subject matter experts, guiding the definition of new requirements and identifying practical ways to improve business processes. Produce technical/functional specifications, workflow charts, and diagrams that provide developers with detailed application requirements. Maintain documentation covering program development, logic, coding, testing, changes, and defect resolution. Identify business strategies, challenges, and opportunities to help partners prioritize new initiatives and capabilities. Collaborate with or lead cross-functional teams to meet business requirements, resolve issues and support system testing. Perform data analysis using E1 queries, Microsoft Pivot tables, etc. for troubleshooting and identification of issues. Create OMW projects to track version changes/enhancements needed for approvals per SDLC requirements. Perform basic SQL queries and write select and update statements needed for data fixes approved per SOX control. Ability to design and map third-party integrations, including EDI and APIs. Develop scenarios, use cases and participate in quality assurance to confirm requirements are implemented correctly. Create user training materials and partner with the business to train end users. Provide technical support for questions, errors, and system issues. Travel is expected to be infrequent, but up to 20% may be required as needed. Account reconciliation support as required by the accounting team. review_candidates.title: Analyste de Projet et de Coordination Terrain [Ouvert aux candidats de Niveaux 1 & 2]
review_candidates.description: Job Description Approche Tiers Conformément à L'engagement Pris De Préserver Les Capacités Et De Soutenir Le Personnel Déjà En Poste Au Sein De L'Organisation, La Majorité Des Postes Vacants Au PNUD, Au FENU Et Au Programme VNU Sont Publiés Selon Un Processus De Candidature à Plusieurs Niveaux, Dans Le Cadre Duquel Niveau 0 : Personnel international du PNUD/FENU/VNU titulaire d'un contrat permanent (PA) ou à durée déterminée (FTA), dont les postes seront supprimés, ou dont les contrats seront résiliés ou non renouvelés en 2026 Niveau 1 : Autre personnel du PNUD/FENU/VNU titulaire d'un contrat permanent (PA) ou à durée déterminée (FTA) Niveau 2 : Personnel du PNUD/FENU/VNU titulaire d'un contrat temporaire (TA), personnel sous contrat PSA régulier, et Volontaires des Nations Unies Experts et Spécialistes Niveau 3 ou aucun niveau indiqué : Tous les autres types de contrat du PNUD/FENU/VNU et d'autres agences, ainsi que les candidats externes Veuillez prendre note du ou des niveaux indiqués dans l'intitulé du poste vacant, le cas échéant, et vous assurer que vous remplissez les conditions requises pour postuler. Background Le Programme des Nations Unies pour le développement (PNUD) est le réseau mondial de développement du système des Nations Unies. Présent dans de nombreux pays, il accompagne les États dans la recherche et la mise en œuvre de solutions adaptées aux défis nationaux et mondiaux en matière de développement. À travers son expertise, ses ressources et son réseau de partenaires, le PNUD contribue au renforcement des capacités nationales, à la promotion d’un développement inclusif et durable ainsi qu’à l’amélioration des conditions de vie des populations. Le Niger fait face à un ensemble de facteurs de fragilité interdépendants, notamment l’insécurité et les violences armées, les conflits communautaires, les déplacements forcés, les inégalités socio-économiques, la faiblesse des capacités institutionnelles et locales, l’accès inégal aux services publics essentiels, le chômage et la vulnérabilité des jeunes, l’exclusion de certains groupes sociaux, ainsi que les effets croissants du changement climatique. Ces facteurs se renforcent mutuellement et affectent particulièrement les régions exposées aux conflits et aux déplacements, notamment Tillabéri, Tahoua et Agadez. Ils compromettent la cohésion sociale, la confiance entre les populations et les institutions, les moyens d’existence et les perspectives de développement durable. Dans ce contexte, le PNUD Niger, en partenariat avec le Gouvernement du Niger, met en œuvre le projet « Renforcement de la Stabilité et du Relèvement Socio-économique dans les régions de Tillabéri, Tahoua et Agadez (2026-2030) ». Le projet constitue une intervention stratégique de stabilisation et de relèvement visant à agir de manière intégrée sur les facteurs de fragilité et à consolider les acquis des interventions antérieures du PNUD, notamment ceux issus du Mécanisme de stabilisation du Liptako-Gourma. Le projet s’inscrit dans le cadre du Programme Intégré Gouvernance (PIG-Niger), du Document de Programme Pays (CPD) du PNUD, du Cadre de coopération des Nations Unies pour le développement durable (UNSDCF), du Plan stratégique du PNUD et des priorités nationales, notamment le Programme pour la Refondation de la République et les orientations nationales en matière de gouvernance, de paix, de sécurité, de développement local et de résilience. L’intervention est structurée autour de trois résultats complémentaires : (i) le renforcement de la cohésion sociale, de la prévention des conflits, de la réconciliation communautaire et de la prévention de l’extrémisme violent ; (ii) l’amélioration de l’accès inclusif, équitable et sécurisé aux services publics et sociaux essentiels et le renforcement de la gouvernance locale ; et (iii) le renforcement du relèvement socio-économique et des moyens d’existence, avec une attention particulière aux femmes, aux jeunes, aux personnes déplacées internes, aux ex-associés aux groupes armés et aux autres groupes vulnérables. C’est dans cette optique que le bureau pays du PNUD au Niger recrute un/une Analyste de Projet et de Coordination Terrain, qui jouera un rôle clé dans la coordination des activités terrain, la liaison avec les partenaires et le renforcement des capacités des acteurs locaux dans les régions ciblées. Le PNUD adopte une approche de portefeuille afin de s’adapter à l’évolution des besoins et de tirer parti des liens entre les interventions pour atteindre ses objectifs stratégiques. En conséquence, le personnel du PNUD est appelé à travailler de manière transversale entre unités, fonctions, équipes et projets, au sein d’équipes pluridisciplinaires favorisant la collaboration horizontale. new_matches.title: Chief Financial Officer
new_matches.description: CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER (CFO) — CAPITAL & PROJECT FINANCE Kamen Construction Limited | Abuja, Nigeria | Full-Time About Kamen Kamen Construction Limited is a Nigerian infrastructure development and construction company delivering roads, drainage, water, electrical infrastructure, buildings and other integrated infrastructure solutions. Through  Kamen Infrastructure Development Services (KAMEN-IDS) , Kamen is developing a structured infrastructure delivery and financing platform that enables governments, real estate developers, corporate organisations, communities and private clients to deliver infrastructure through flexible financing arrangements. As we enter our next phase of growth, we are seeking a commercially driven and highly capable  Chief Financial Officer (CFO)  to lead our financial strategy, capital raising, project finance, investment structuring, treasury and financial governance. This is  not a conventional accounting-focused CFO position . We are looking for a finance leader who can help build Kamen's financial architecture, raise equity and debt, establish project SPVs, structure infrastructure transactions and develop strong relationships with banks, investors, capital houses and institutional funding partners. The Role The CFO will be a key member of Kamen's executive management team and will report directly to the Managing Director/CEO. The successful candidate will lead the company's corporate finance strategy while serving as the financial champion for  KAMEN-IDS and its project-financing platform . The role combines corporate finance, capital raising, project finance, treasury, investment management and financial governance. Key Responsibilities 1. Corporate Finance & Strategy Develop and execute Kamen's financial strategy and capital structure. Lead budgeting, forecasting, financial modelling and capital allocation. Provide the CEO and Board with financial and strategic decision support. Improve profitability, cash generation and return on invested capital. Establish strong financial controls, policies and governance. 2. Capital Raising & Investor Relations Develop and execute Kamen's equity and debt capital-raising strategy. Identify and build relationships with private equity funds, infrastructure funds, family offices, banks, development finance institutions, institutional investors, private credit funds and capital-market operators. Prepare investment teasers, information memoranda, financial models and investor presentations. Lead investor discussions, due diligence and transaction negotiations. Build and manage a pipeline of potential investors and financing partners. Lead successful equity investment transactions for Kamen and its projects. 3. KAMEN-IDS Project Finance & SPVs Develop the financial architecture for KAMEN-IDS. Establish and manage appropriate Project Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs). Structure project-level financing and determine the appropriate mix of equity, debt, client contributions, supplier credit and other funding sources. Develop detailed project financial models covering construction costs, cash flow, revenues, financing costs, profitability, IRR, DSCR, payback and sensitivity analysis. Assess the bankability of projects before financial commitment. Coordinate financial close and project-financing processes. Ensure project funds are appropriately ring-fenced and controlled. Monitor the financial performance of project SPVs. 4. Debt, Debentures & Structured Finance Lead Kamen's debt-financing initiatives. Develop relationships with banks, investment firms, capital houses and private credit providers. Structure and negotiate corporate loans, project finance, debentures, private debt, asset-backed financing, receivables-backed financing, bridge financing and other structured-finance facilities. Negotiate financing terms including pricing, tenor, security, covenants and repayment structures. Coordinate lender due diligence and financial documentation. 5. Treasury & Cash Flow Lead Kamen's treasury function and group-wide cash management. Establish rolling cash-flow forecasts and liquidity controls. Optimise working capital and cash conversion. Manage banking relationships and financing facilities. Ensure proper utilisation of project funds and timely debt servicing. Establish early-warning indicators for liquidity and financial risk. 6. Financial Reporting, Risk & Governance Lead the Finance & Accounts function and ensure accurate and timely management reporting. Strengthen budgeting, variance analysis, receivables and payables management. Coordinate audits, tax compliance and statutory reporting. Develop financial risk-management and internal-control systems. Ensure effective financial governance across Kamen and its project SPVs. 7. Leadership Build and lead a high-performance Finance, Treasury, Investment and Capital Management team. Establish clear KPIs and accountability. Work closely with Projects, Commercial, Procurement, Business Development and Operations to ensure projects are commercially viable and properly funded. Key Performance Measures The CFO will be measured primarily by business outcomes, including: Equity capital successfully raised. Debt and debenture financing successfully secured. Number and value of financing transactions closed. Capital raised for KAMEN-IDS projects. Number of project SPVs established and financed. Successful financial closes. Cost and structure of capital achieved. Project profitability and return on capital. Cash-flow and liquidity performance. Quality of investor and lender relationships. Strength of financial controls and reporting. Qualifications & Experience Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration or related discipline. Professional qualification such as  ACA, ACCA, CFA, CIMA  or equivalent. Minimum  10–15 years' relevant experience , including substantial senior-management experience. Proven experience in corporate finance, project finance, investment banking, structured finance or infrastructure financing. Demonstrable experience raising equity and/or debt capital. Strong financial-modelling and transaction-structuring skills. Experience negotiating with banks, investors and capital providers. Strong understanding of Nigerian financial and capital markets. Experience in  construction, infrastructure, real estate, private equity, private credit, development finance or investment banking  will be highly advantageous. The Ideal Candidate We are looking for a  builder, not just a financial controller . The ideal candidate must be commercially astute, entrepreneurial, analytical and highly skilled in financial modelling, deal structuring and negotiation. He or she should be comfortable engaging CEOs, investors, fund managers, bankers, government stakeholders and other sophisticated capital providers. Most importantly, candidates must demonstrate  actual transactions completed , not simply experience preparing financial reports. Candidates who have personally led or materially contributed to successful equity raises, debt transactions, debentures, project-finance deals or investment transactions will have a significant advantage. Our Expectation Within the first 12–18 months, the CFO should help Kamen transition from a predominantly construction-company financing model toward an  institutional infrastructure-financing platform , capable of: Originate → Structure → Finance → Execute → Monitor → Recycle Capital across a growing portfolio of infrastructure projects. Application Interested candidates should submit a detailed CV highlighting their experience in  capital raising, corporate finance, project finance, investment banking, debt/equity transactions, and infrastructure financing . Candidates should clearly identify significant transactions they have personally led or materially contributed to, including the approximate value and nature of each transaction.

Ensure compliance with safety regulation, building codes, project specification and stakeholder expectations. Coordinate with contractors, suppliers and stakeholders to ensure deliverables are clearly defended and expectations are being met to keep the project on schedule and within budget. new_matches.description: Job Brief (Re-advertise) KINETIK is seeking qualified professionals for the role of Deputy Director Financing and Delivery to support program delivery and implementation in Jakarta, Indonesia. Deputy Director Financing and Delivery Program Background KINETIK, the Australia-Indonesia Climate and Sustainable Infrastructure Partnership, supports Indonesia to strengthen sustainable infrastructure systems, mobilise climate-aligned investment, and advance low-emissions and climate-resilient development. Working with the Government of Indonesia (GOI) and a broad network of public and private partners, the program seeks to expand investment in sustainable infrastructure while ensuring the inclusion of local communities, particularly women, girls and people with disabilities. KINETIK contributes to three inter-related End of Program Outcomes (EOPOs): Climate resilience: Investments from government, private and community actors increasingly contribute to climate mitigation and adaptation in Indonesia. Innovative financing: GOI increasingly uses diverse, innovative and high-quality financing to support inclusive, climate-resilient development. Sustainable infrastructure: GOI delivers sustainable and resilient economic infrastructure, particularly in water, transport and energy, that meets the needs of communities, including women, people with disabilities and marginalised groups. The program builds on long-standing Australia-Indonesia cooperation in infrastructure and climate policy. It promotes locally led development, integrates gender equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI), and works with development finance and private sector partners to mobilise investment and support sustainable infrastructure systems across sectors including renewable energy, water, sanitation and waste management, and sustainable transport. KINETIK is supported by the Australian Government’s Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) and implemented by DT Global. About DT Global Asia Pacific At DT Global Asia Pacific, we aim to positively impact people’s lives through delivery excellence. As a leading implementing partner across Asia and the Pacific, we co-create locally led solutions in partnership with governments, communities, and stakeholders. We bring together talented teams and deep regional expertise to deliver initiatives that promote inclusive economic growth, essential services, and resilient, secure communities. With over 1,500 staff, experts in 22+ countries and more than 60 years of development experience, we tackle complex community, national and transnational challenges — from governance and justice systems to climate resilience, infrastructure and social equity — with innovative thinking and a commitment to long-term impact. For more information, please see www.dt-global.com The Role The Deputy Director Financing and Delivery (DD F&D) is a senior executive position responsible for KINETIK’s Financing and Delivery pillar, encompassing infrastructure, climate-resilient development, and investment mobilisation. The role provides strategic portfolio-wide leadership across the F&D pillar, ensuring effective delivery of climate-resilient investments and mobilisation of climate-aligned financing across the full KINETIK partnership. The role is accountable for ensuring that KINETIK delivers a credible, investment-oriented portfolio that translates policy ambition into financed and implementable outcomes The role is accountable for setting the strategic direction and performance of KINETIK’s Financing and Delivery pillar, ensuring that priority infrastructure and climate opportunities progress from early-stage identification through to financing and implementation. This includes overseeing the development of a coherent pipeline aligned with Government of Indonesia priorities, DFAT objectives, and KINETIK’s EOPOs, and ensuring that infrastructure, climate, and financing elements are effectively sequenced end-to-end. Financing within KINETIK refers to translating climate and infrastructure opportunities into investible and implementable outcomes. KINETIK will do this in two ways. First, through supporting priority GoI climate and infrastructure projects through project preparation, investment readiness, financial and commercial structuring, mobilisation of capital and development of innovative financing approaches through government, development finance and private sector partners. Second, through private sector development based approaches, working to build Indonesia’s innovative financing ecosystem and capital markets to crowd in additional financing for Indonesia’s climate and infrastructure priorities. The Deputy Director Financing and Delivery provides portfolio-level leadership across this function, including setting priorities, allocating resources, and monitoring performance. Technical execution of financing and transactions activities is led by the Head of Financing and Transactions, while sector delivery is led by the Head of Climate Resilient Development. This role is prioritised for a suitably qualified Indonesian and international candidates with strong public and/or private finance credentials and established networks with Indonesian government and financial institutions. Candidates with demonstrated senior leadership experience in infrastructure, climate finance, or development finance are strongly encouraged to apply. As a member of the Executive Leadership Team (ELT), the DD F&D contributes to strategic decision-making and program governance. The role coordinates with the Deputy Director Policy, Partnerships, and Inclusion (PPI) to ensure end-to-end coherence across sector engagement, from policy and regulatory reform through to financing and delivery, and leads engagement with DFAT on Financing and Delivery matters. The DD F&D enables sector Leads (covering Renewable Energy, Sustainable Transport and Urban Connectivity, as well as Water, Sanitation and Solid Waste) to engage across KINETIK on policy, partnerships, and inclusion relevant to their sectors, and orchestrates cross-pillar sequencing where required. KINETIK senior leadership roles are currently being recruited concurrently. DT Global will consider candidates across aligned technical and management profiles, with final role configuration and responsibilities calibrated to ensure the strongest overall leadership team composition across the Financing and Delivery, Climate Resilient Development, and Financing and Transactions functions. Click on the link or copy paste it to access the full Terms of Reference for this position: https://tinyurl.com/depdirfd About You Essential Experience and Knowledge Postgraduate qualification in engineering, finance, economics, environmental science, or a related field. Minimum 15 years of experience in infrastructure, climate finance, or development finance, including significant experience at senior leadership level on large, complex programs or within government/financial institutions. Extensive senior-level experience in infrastructure financing, investment mobilisation, transaction advisory, innovative financing, blended finance and/or sustainable finance, including engagement with government, development finance institutions, commercial financiers or institutional investors. DT Global welcomes applications from individuals with diverse backgrounds including First Nations peoples, diverse Sexual Orientation, Gender Identity and Expression, and Sex Characteristics (SOGIESC), and people with disabilities. The Role You will oversee data systems and analytics for Evidence Action's new In-Line Chlorination Innovation Team, under the Safe Water Now Program. As ILC scales up, core questions remain about how to optimize device performance, reduce operational costs, and strengthen community engagement. Answering these questions well will shape whether ILC can become a scalable, cost-effective model reaching millions more people. new_matches.description: GiveDirectly has delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty across 15 countries since 2011. We believe cash transfers are one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid, with the research to back it up. Our work has been covered by The Economist, NPR, TED, and The Washington Post. We are one of Time100’s Most Influential Companies of 2026. Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical. We support high ownership and real professional growth. Curious about what it's really like to work here? Read our values and hear from the people who do. If they resonate, this could be a great fit! About This Role The Risk Management Program Manager is responsible for preventing, detecting, mitigating and investigating the field-based risks associated with delivering millions of dollars to thousands of poor households across a portfolio of countries. The Program Manager (PM) will work with the Internal Audit Director and the wider Internal Audit team to design innovations to manage the risks associated with cash transfers. Reports to: Director, Internal Audit Level : Manager Location: Remote - Goma/Bukavu/Kinshasa, DRC with a requirement to overlap with an East Africa timezone by at least 3 hours. Role Summary Supports overall Global Internal Audit (IA) strategy. Overall risk manager for the countries in their portfolio. In partnership with the Country Director (CD), lead the development of the country IA strategy. Supports on all project design at all stages (project inception, proposal creation, project design, risk register creation, ongoing project risk management, project closure). Leads (or where relevant, delegates) all country syncs with CD. HR oversight (not direct management) for all countries in their portfolio. Takes direct lead on certain, more sensitive and high risk investigations in portfolio (as determined by CD and IAD). Manages Internal Audit for each country in their portfolio Manages Internal Audit Manager (IAM) directly. Supports admin oversight and procurement for the IA team in country (ensuring docs are in order etc). Carries out regular spot checks on country operations and ensures IAM is doing their checks and documenting them. Seeks to develop and analyze data we have but also look for new ways to spot and reduce fraud. Visible point of contact for country team and part of country management team where relevant. Leads coordination with other internal teams (such as Safeguarding, Programs, and Tech) as well as external partners, such as Telcos where needed. Visits each country in portfolio at least 1x per year for field visits. Roles And Responsibilities Project Design (25%) Represent IA in country project design conversations, including development of strategic risk management measures. Owning development of project-specific Internal Audit proposals detailing audit rates, audit approaches, e.t.c. for new projects and discussing these with CD. Oversee community risk scoping exercises and ensure full scoping report is submitted to IAD and CDs for all new projects. Ensure that customized risk registers are created for all new projects; ensure that risk registers for ongoing projects are updated regularly. Review implementation tools, e.g. enrollment surveys, to better align them to risk detection, mitigation and prevention. Systems Orientated risk monitoring (45%) Owning and monitoring IA metrics / KPIs in countries of portfolio and owning correction of dropping or critically missed metrics. Overall owner (accountable) of country project workbooks detailing workplans and staffing, tech related requirements and activity timelines. Define and review risk classifications based on projects and country level activities. Hold weekly (or bi-weekly) meetings with Country Directors in each country you are assigned. Lead the development of escalation protocols for different types of risks and monitor implementation of the protocols by country managers. Lead the transparent, accountable and where needed collaborative investigation of high risk cases. Support the IAM to undertake community based fraud intelligence monitoring exercises and escalate any identified risk trends to the CD and IAD. Monitor the traffic and trends of risk reporting and flag high risk countries and projects to the CD and IAD. Support the IAD with tech-related fraud prevention innovations work through different inputs as may be requested from time to time. Where relevant, build in-country relationships with fraud management stakeholders (for example, MoMo provider telcos) for sustainable fraud resolutions in-country. Conduct spot checks on both the programs and IA operations to ensure high quality and identify any abnormalities. Build and manage in-country project related stakeholder relationships; working with different in-country teams to ensure IA deliverables are tracked as per workplan. Write and share with the IA - Director, quarterly productivity reports and/or project specific retrospectives (or progress reports). People Management (10%) Directly manages Internal Audit Managers in all countries you are assigned. Conduct regular check-ins with Direct Reports. Conduct performance reviews for direct reports every quarter and provide a report of the same to the IA-Director and CD where relevant. Indirectly support the AFMs and FOs in the countries you are assigned. Develop a team with a high capacity for problem solving, critical thinking, and strong analytical and communication skill. Conduct regular skip-level meetings with AFMs. Hiring: Directly responsible for hiring IAMs in the countries you are assigned. Create a strong overall team Manage conflicts and other risks within the team and escalate where appropriate. Promote effective team culture by encouraging recognition of positive achievements and other team-building initiatives. Model ethical behavior that encourages the team to report misconduct within GD staff, partners, community and recipients. Conduct staff career growth needs assessments (through structures surveys and 1:1 sessions) and liaise with the HR manager to deliver robust professional development sessions internally and externally. Culture Building (10%) Act as the custodian of ‘Recipients First’ Value within the team by ensuring compliance to policies and protocols of GiveDirectly. Maintain an active, visible and consistent commitment to a common standard of behavior that is required throughout every aspect of the organization as stipulated in the Code of Conduct Statement. Manage a team that is driven by individual accountability involving moving beyond corporate ‘rules-based’ behavior to ‘values-based’ behavior that promotes a greater focus on promoting individual integrity.” Identify sub-cultures within the organization that may result in safeguarding and fraud risks to recipients. Conduct annual training to country Programs teams on fraud and safeguarding mitigation requirements as outlined in GD policies. Other responsibilities (10%) Supports Director on reflecting on and rethinking the Global IA strategy and mandate. Supports Director on utilizing AI and technology to improve GD’s fraud risk management systems. Participates in weekly IA management meetings and weekly sprints to discuss cross-team activities. Support on country external audits where requested. Support on non-field based fraud management on an as-needed basis in your countries of operation. Proactively identify and flag ways to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of IA’s operations. Support other country of operations outside of portfolio where necessary. What You’ll Bring Internal audit / risk management background - 3+ years leading audit, compliance, or risk functions, ideally in a role that combined strategy design with hands-on fieldwork (not just desk audits). Fraud investigation experience - has personally led or overseen sensitive/high-risk investigations, not just routine checks. People management - directly managed a team, including hiring, performance reviews, and conflict management. Cross-country or multi-site portfolio experience - managed risk/audit across several countries or regional units simultaneously, since this role owns a country portfolio. Field-based operations exposure - comfortable with in-person field visits (at least 1x/year per country) in low-resource or humanitarian/development settings, not purely office-based audit work. Stakeholder management - experience liaising with external partners and internal cross-functional teams (Safeguarding, Programs, Tech). Data/analytics fluency - experience using data to detect fraud trends, build KPIs/metrics, and monitor risk reporting, plus openness to AI/tech-driven fraud prevention tools. Program/project design experience - has contributed to project design, risk registers, and proposal creation, ideally in an NGO, cash-transfer, or development-sector context. Report writing at a senior level - track record producing strategy documents, quarterly reports, and retrospectives for leadership. Fluency in both English and Portuguese. Alignment with GiveDirectly Values and active demonstration of our core competencies: emotional intelligence, problem solving, project management, follow-through, and fostering inclusivity. Why work at GiveDirectly? Role At GiveDirectly, we work to ensure that you have everything you need to excel in your role and on your team, including: A positive and supportive team with opportunities for advancement A demonstrated commitment to helping all staff develop and grow A competitive salary, including bonus A robust health benefits plan (exact details will vary by country) Unlimited PTO (that we encourage staff to take!) Read more about our ongoing diversity, equity, and inclusion efforts here and about our decision to move our central support teams to remote first here . Compensation At GiveDirectly, we strive to pay our employees generously and equitably. We use an accredited third party salary aggregator to calculate what we believe to be competitive pay based on role, location, and cost of living. We also have a no negotiation policy to ensure we are paying staff equitably across roles. Read more about our compensation philosophy here . Unless otherwise noted, the benefits stipend may be used to cover benefits or taken as additional taxable income. Base Salary: $ 75,100 Bonus at Target Performance: 10% (~$ 7,510 with potential for upside. Flagging for US applicants: We invite you to "Know Your Rights" as an applicant. Commitment to Safeguarding As a global organization working with communities to eliminate extreme poverty, GiveDirectly takes the safeguarding of its recipients, staff, and partners seriously. To that end, GiveDirectly is a member of the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, and will systematically check with previous employers about any abuse or misconduct related matters involving potential new hires. We may also employ other robust pre-hire screens, including in-depth reference checks, criminal background checks, and sanctions screens. These efforts help us continue to build and maintain trust with the communities we work with, and prevent abuse to our recipients and staff. **GD is committed to observing all local, national and international laws that protect people and basic human rights of all. GD is committed to a policy of “zero tolerance when it comes to preventing, reporting, or responding to any form of abuse or exploitation.” and expects anyone who works for GD to uphold the protection and safeguarding of our recipients as a priority.** Reasonable Accommodations We are committed to fostering an inclusive and accessible work environment. If you require any accommodations during the application or interview process, or to perform the essential functions of the role, please email us at careers@givedirectly.org with the email subject “Accommodation Needed”. new_matches.title: Head of HR Programmes
new_matches.description: Job Title: Head of HR Programmes Location: UK, Remote (some travel to HALO’s international programmes required) Hours: Full Time Contract Type: Permanent Salary: Competitive, dependent on experience Reports To: HR Director Direct Reports: IHRMs Key Internal Contacts/Relationships: Head of HR Operations, HR Operations Team, Talent Acquisition Team, Head of Talent & Performance, ER, Programme Directors and Programme Managers, CFO, Finance, UK/HQ Functional Leads, Central support functions, ExCo (as required) Key External Contacts/Relationships: Suppliers Job Purpose: To provide senior strategic HR partnership to HALO's international programmes, supporting programme leaders to manage workforce, employee relations, safeguarding and organisational capability issues effectively across complex operating environments, while ensuring alignment with organisational policies, values and legal obligations. The role provides an auditable route for escalation of complex or sensitive employment, conduct or safeguarding issues. The role holder ensures that people decisions affecting international programme staff are proportionate, timely and grounded in operational reality, while safeguarding independence from programme management and maintaining consistent standards of HR support across regions. About HALO HALO is the leading global NGO addressing the impact and drivers of conflict in 30 countries and territories, with over 8,000 staff. Most of our staff are local employees and include a growing number of women. Our primary duty is to serve people affected by conflict, clearing landmines and the explosive remnants of war that threaten lives and livelihoods long after fighting has finished. We make land safe where war has ended, while also assisting those affected by active conflict and endemic violence. HALO addresses human suffering caused by armed violence in some of the world’s most fragile places, securing weapons and ammunition and working with both state and community actors to reduce the prevalence of armed violence. About The Role The role covers all HR partnering activity for HALO's country programmes. It operates across multiple jurisdictions and employment frameworks and within varied funding models, including grant funded and fixed period contractual arrangements. The role does not hold line management accountability for country (national) teams. Authority is exercised through professional judgement, influence and established governance, including determining escalation and acting as the senior HR adviser on complex people, safeguarding and workforce matters across HALO's programmes. Responsibilities Strategic People Partnership: Act as the senior HR partner to programme leadership on workforce, employee relations, leadership and organisational capability matters. Support programme leaders to design and apply employment and contracting arrangements that are proportionate to programme duration, funding terms and operational need. Provide senior level HR advice that supports programme leaders to operate effectively in complex, resource constrained environments. Oversee workforce planning and contracting approaches suited to different operating contexts, ensuring structures remain flexible enough for programmes to scale capacity up and down as operational need changes. Employee Relations And Safeguarding Act as the senior HR partner to programme leadership on complex people, safeguarding and duty of care matters, providing expert, decision-focused advice that supports timely and proportionate resolution, but with programme leadership retaining ownership of decisions and outcomes. Support programme leaders to anticipate and address people challenges arising in fragile, high-risk and resource-constrained operating environments. Maintain oversight of significant people and safeguarding matters across programmes, ensuring consistency of approach, proportionality of response and appropriate escalation in line with organisational standards. Ensure that significant people and safeguarding considerations are appropriately communicated to Executive and Board stakeholders, with clear articulation of context, options and mitigations. Policy Application And Standards Interpret and apply global HR policies within diverse local and legal contexts, exercising professional judgement where policy intent, donor conditions and operational reality intersect. Support programme leadership to understand and meet their legal, safeguarding and people-management obligations across multiple jurisdictions, balancing compliance with operational effectiveness. Assurance And Risk Support the delivery of the HR assurance programme through reviews of workforce practices, employee relations, safeguarding, duty of care and people management arrangements across programmes. Provide professional judgement on programme-level workforce risks, control effectiveness and compliance with organisational standards, identifying themes, emerging risks and improvement opportunities. Support programme leadership to implement agreed corrective actions and strengthen people management practices following assurance reviews. Leadership And Capability Development Strengthen people management capability across programmes through coaching/mentoring, advice and support on complex workforce, employee relations matters, training, performance, development and succession planning. Support programme leaders to apply organisational people policies and processes confidently and consistently. Manage and develop the Regional HR network, ensuring consistent regional support, visibility of ER and safeguarding matters, and early intervention on emerging issues. Ensure HALO’s values and standards are reflected consistently in people decisions and leadership behaviour across programme teams. Interface With HR Operations Act as the primary interface between programme teams and HR Operations, ensuring workforce challenges, operational realities and programme feedback inform the continuous improvement of HR policies, systems and processes, and supporting the consistent application of organisational standards across programmes. Work jointly with the Head of HR Operations to maintain common standards, shared escalation routes and a joined-up approach to case handling across the organisation. General Uphold HALO’s core values and standards, promoting its ethos and mission statement. Ensure familiarity with and adherence to all HALO policies and procedures, especially the code of conduct and safeguarding Travel Requirements Occasional travel to programmes globally Requirements Technical / Professional: Significant leadership experience, including in international, multi-jurisdictional or complex operating environments. Demonstrable experience of managing remote teams effectively across multiple countries or regions. Experience providing senior level advice to non-HR leadership and operating with autonomy in ambiguous or fast-moving situations. Ability to calibrate HR responses appropriately, distinguishing between complex, high-risk cases and matters that can be resolved pragmatically and proportionately. Deep expertise in employee relations, safeguarding and managing complex people issues in international environments. Strong understanding of UK employment law and law across multiple jurisdictions. Advanced professional judgement in ambiguous, high-risk environments. Ability to translate complex risk into clear, decision focused advice. Strong understanding of embedding a safeguarding assurance framework. Behavioural / Leadership High credibility and gravitas with senior operational leaders. Influential without authority; confident challenger. Calm, measured and values-led under pressure. Strong ethical judgement and organisational awareness. Ability to develop and lead HR teams across multiple jurisdictions. Desirable Requirements Experience working within a not-for-profit / global matrix organisation. International employment law knowledge Benefits 25 days’ annual leave plus 8 statutory holidays Non-contributory life assurance Private medical insurance Pension contributions matched by HALO up to 5% Emergency medical insurance while travelling overseas Flexible working policy Please submit a CV (no more than 2 pages) and a cover letter (no more than 1 page) outlining how your experience matches the key skills and competencies required by 24th September 2026. Applications without a cover letter tailored to this position will not be considered. We reserve the right to amend the closing date depending on the number of applications received. The HALO Trust is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate against any applicant for employment because of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, or sexual orientation. The HALO Trust is committed to attracting, developing, and retaining talented individuals from a wide range of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. The HALO Trust is committed to ensuring that it provides a safe and trusted environment which safeguards and promotes the welfare and wellbeing of anyone who comes into contact with, or is part of, the Charity, with a zero-tolerance approach to behaviours which challenge this.

Operations & Logistics Manage venue selection, site inspections and event logistics. Coordinate event setup, rehearsals, production and dismantling. Oversee guest management, hospitality, transportation and entertainment requirements. Coordinate event staffing and operational requirements. Team Leadership Lead and coordinate internal event and project teams. Allocate resources according to project requirements. Monitor team performance and project delivery. Develop a collaborative, accountable and high-performance working environment. Build and maintain a network of experienced freelance event professionals where required. 10. Regional Management Support the development and growth of the company's Middle East operation. Represent the company professionally within the UAE luxury and events industry. Develop strategic relationships with key industry stakeholders. Monitor the competitive landscape and market opportunities. Provide management with regular updates on projects, business opportunities and market developments. Contribute to the development of the company's Middle East strategy. Candidate Requirements Education Bachelor's degree in Event Management, Marketing, Business Administration, Hospitality, Communications, Public Relations or a related field . Additional qualifications in event management, luxury brand management, marketing or experiential marketing would be advantageous. Professional Experience 8–15+ years of experience in luxury events, experiential marketing, event production, creative agencies or a related environment. Proven experience managing high-end luxury events and brand experiences . Experience working with fashion, jewellery, luxury watches, beauty, hospitality or premium lifestyle brands . Strong UAE/Middle East market experience. Experience dealing with international brands and senior-level clients. Previous experience managing teams, suppliers and complex projects. Strong commercial and business-development exposure. Candidates coming from luxury event agencies, experiential agencies, creative agencies, fashion houses, jewellery companies, luxury watch brands, premium hospitality or luxury retail would be highly relevant. new_matches.title: Coordinator, Digital Health (Ethiopia)
new_matches.description: This role was posted on August 13, 2026. Please note that we will review applications on a rolling basis. About Last Mile Health Last Mile Health saves lives in the world's most remote communities. Our vision is a health worker within reach of everyone, everywhere. We partner with governments to recruit, train, equip, and integrate professional community health workers into national health systems, equipping them to deliver quality primary care in rural and remote communities. Founded in Liberia in 2007, we now operate programs in Ethiopia, Liberia, Sierra Leone, and Malawi. Our global offices are located in Accra, Ghana and in the United States. We are looking for mission-driven leaders to join us as we work to ensure no patient is out of reach. About The Ethiopia Team The Ethiopia team works in partnership with Ethiopia’s Ministry of Health to strengthen the country’s flagship Health Extension Program, a globally recognized model for delivering primary healthcare through more than 40,000 Health Extension Workers. Led by Abraham Zerihun, the team works to upskill the Health Extension Workers through blended learning that combines digital and in-person training. It also advances digital innovation through HEP Assist, an AI-powered clinical decision-support tool that helps Health Extension Workers provide evidence-based care at the point of service. The team's portfolio spans maternal, newborn, child health, nutrition, and non-communicable diseases, including hypertension, diabetes, eye care, and stroke prevention and management, while strengthening health systems through sustainable community health financing, resource mapping, and strategic planning to support long-term government leadership and program sustainability. The Role At Last Mile Health (LMH), we make bold commitments that inspire innovation. Do you have experience supporting digital health implementation, troubleshooting technology in the field, and working with frontline health workers to deploy and strengthen digital health solutions? If so, you may be the next Digital Health Coordinator at Last Mile Health. The Digital Health Coordinators will provide high level technical and implementation support for the deployment of LMH's digital health tools to Community Health Workers (CHWs) across Ethiopia, including Extension Essentials and HEP Assist AI. Reporting to the Director, Digital Health, Ethiopia, the Coordinators will support planning, coordination, and implementation of digital health activities, working closely with program teams, field teams, and users to ensure effective adoption and use of digital health solutions. Based in Addis Ababa, the role will provide hands-on support to digital health implementation and will travel to different regions as needed to support field deployment and training activities. The Coordinators will support workplan management, data collection and feedback processes, data analysis and dashboard development, application installation and troubleshooting, and the development and implementation of processes and procedures that strengthen digital health activities. The role will also provide remote technical support to users through phone, email, and relevant open source digital health communities. This advertisement is for two Digital Health Coordinator positions based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. This is a fixed-term position for 24–36 months, with the potential for renewal. The role is based onsite in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, and is open only to candidates who are currently located in and authorized to work in Ethiopia. What You'll Do Digital Health Solutions Implementation Coordination Coordinate with the Senior Digital Health Coordinators to ensure that the digital health initiatives are run successfully across all districts Work with the Director, Digital Health, Senior Manager of Digital Health, Ethiopia country office program team, the Global DH Manager, and other relevant internal LMH departments (MERL, HSS, etc.) to maintain and update deployment tasks in the implementation plan Roll out new Deployment Packages (latest apps and tools such as Extension Essentials and HEP Assist AI) to Health Extension Workers (HEWs) Support establishment of a digital health management processes and procedures for digital health activities Support Digital Health Training activities including the planning and deployment of a digital education platform for Health Extension Workers Coordinate, facilitate and participate in health worker and health systems leaders trainings across districts Support learners (health workers, Ministry of Health (MOH) and health system leaders) during training (including app installation on mobile device, etc.) and remotely after training Support LMH and MOH program managers/ Coordinators in creating user accounts for app access and maintain dashboards to track learners sync status and course performance Support data collection efforts for all digital health activities including data tracking, data review and date submission support Ensure that all users have functioning equipment during training and support immediate troubleshooting of devices during activity deployments Support the Director, Digital Health to communicate LMH digital health priorities, and provide training on essential digital health skills to LMH and MoH team members when applicable Test and Innovate New Solutions for The Ethiopian Health Extension Program (HEP) When necessary, update course content in moodle as requested by the Programs team. This may require quick edits, quality assurance, and publishing of course materials. Quality assurance (particularly) regression testing (testing of new features in new releases) of software before launch Feedback provision and gathering on releases (testing releases, post-release) Identify and report bugs through LMH’s tracking systems (Jira), and on the Oppia Mobile Community website Test new plug-ins, alternative learning platforms, and assess the suitability of different digital health software and hardware for the national HEW program Support the Senior Software Engineer to configure learning software and support the integration and migration between systems as requested Understand and troubleshoot technical issues in the field and report them to the Senior Digital Health Coordinators and Senior Software Engineer Brainstorm and test innovations such as experimental hardware, forms, and digital interventions related to LMH’s digital health platform When necessary, participate in field visits to observe digital health team processes (including device management, follow-up data collection, feedback gathering) and generate ideas for improvement Draw on technical skills, critical thinking, problem-solving ability, and creativity to provide the technical edge to LMH’s digital health platform What You'll Bring Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field, such as computer science, Information Technology, software engineering, statistics, mathematics with minimum of three years of work experience. Experience working with data systems including data entry, data quality assurance, and data cleaning, relational databases, dashboard development, and monitoring and evaluation Experience with project management, and a high level of initiative Relevant years of experience working on IT-related projects Progressive years of experience designing and implementing Digital Health systems in the field. Willingness and ability to travel to remote areas of Ethiopia, sometimes for overnight visits You'll Impress Us If You are knowledgeable and experienced with community health systems, especially the Ethiopian Health Extension Workers (HEW) program You have the ability to build and edit courses on Moodle LMS You have experience with analyzing data and developing dashboards using data analytics and visualization tools like Data Studio You have verbal and written communication skills for understanding project requirements and explaining these needs to employees and third-party providers You are able to prioritize and manage time to ensure tasks are completed on time We're looking for someone with many of the qualifications listed above, but we know no one meets every requirement. If you're excited about our mission and believe your experience aligns with this role, we encourage you to apply. Compensation information Overview Of Last Mile Health’s Compensation Model At Last Mile Health, we are committed to equitable and transparent compensation. Employees are paid using a clear, consistent methodology that is fully transparent and accessible to everyone. We look forward to answering any questions you may have during the hiring process. Before applying to this role, please take a moment to learn more about our approach to compensation and how compensation works in each of the countries where we operate. Please find the link to our compensation model and benefits overview below: Compensation For This Position The Band for this position: ETH-2 For Ethiopia, the range is an annual gross of $13,094 USD to $24,733 USD, dependent upon experience doing an equivalent role. Please note that compensation is subject to statutory taxes. Benefits Healthcare: Comprehensive health insurance and wellbeing support for you and your dependents. Save for retirement: Retirement options with a 3% employer match, varying by location. Paid time off: Generous paid time off, sick leave, quarterly company holidays, and approximately one week of office closure at the end of the year. Family support: Generous parental leave for employees welcoming a child through birth or adoption. Professional development: Access to technical and leadership development opportunities to support your growth. Mental healthcare: Counselling and resilience services to support employees and their dependents through life’s challenges. We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at Last Mile Health. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. Last Mile Health is a registered 501(c)3 non-profit organization. For more information, visit www.lastmilehealth.org. At Last Mile Health, we are committed to creating a safe and inclusive environment for everyone. If you require assistance or a reasonable accommodation due to a disability during the selection process, please inform the People Operations team member you are engaging with. Any disclosure related to a disability will be kept strictly confidential and used solely to determine appropriate accommodations. Disclosure is entirely voluntary and will not influence hiring decisions or employment opportunities.
